# KeyJawn

> Terminal keyboard tools for Android and iOS

KeyJawn helps people work with remote terminals from a phone. Android and iOS have different features and distribution paths.

## iOS beta

- The public TestFlight invitation is not accepting new testers as of August 28, 2026.
- A revised App Store submission has not been sent.
- The app includes a built-in remote SSH terminal. Commands run on the configured server, not on the phone.
- The keyboard extension enters text and control sequences into the active app. The receiving app decides how to interpret them.
- Basic keyboard input does not need Full Access.
- Full Access is optional. KeyJawn uses it for copied-image upload, shared keyboard settings, user-created shortcuts, or clipboard history.
- Image upload reads one copied image from the pasteboard, prepares it in memory, uploads it with SFTP to a host configured for SSH key authentication, and enters the remote path. Password authentication remains available for terminal connections.
- The iOS app does not request Photos or Files access. The copied-image upload feature does not browse local files or list, read, or download remote files.
- Voice input is available in the built-in terminal, not in the keyboard extension.

## Android

- Android APK releases: https://github.com/jamditis/keyjawn/releases
- KeyJawn Lite has active internal and closed Google Play test tracks. Google Play production is inactive.
- The free APK includes terminal keys, voice input, clipboard history, built-in slash commands, swipe gestures, and per-app autocorrect.
- The $4 Android full APK adds image upload, SSH host management, themes, clipboard pins, and custom command sets.
- The Android purchase does not unlock an iOS product.

## Privacy boundary

- KeyJawn has no developer analytics, ads, or tracking.
- User-started SSH, SFTP, and speech features send only the data needed for the requested operation to the selected server or platform speech service.
- SSH credentials stay in platform-protected device storage.
